newsitem.title: USA: FDA expects to move quickly on ruminant feed rule.
newsitem.headline: FDA expects to move quickly on ruminant feed rule.

text.p: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is likely to move "fairly quickly" in approving a final rule on restricting the feeding of recycled ruminant tissue to other ruminants, an FDA spokeman said Thursday.
"We expect to be able to move fairly quickly," said Lawrence Bachorik of the FDA. "We expect a final rule in a matter of months...this is a priority."

FDA earlier Thursday proposed to ban the feeding of tissues from ruminants to cattle and other ruminants, in an effort to protect American livestock from transmissable degernative neurological diseases and specifically bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), commonly known as mad cow.
Bachorik said the proposed rule will now be published in the Federal Register, and that the public comment period will be 45 days.

While the FDA official said the agency will closely study any new significant information that may be revealed in the public response, he indicated without such significant new findings, there is not likely to be much change in the final rule from today's proposal.
"We feel like we've done a lot of the hard work already," Bachorik said. "We're fairly confident that most of the issues to be considered have been considered."
The FDA action was criticized by some as unnecessary since there has never been a reported case of BSE in the United States.
But Bachorik said the action is warranted even though the risk of the disease is small.
"In essense we're building a firewall against BSE," he said. "The risk is small, but it's real...if a case were to occur, the risk would be very great."
